issues.issue: This unqualified assumption of all inherent risks cannot be squared with c043, which subjects the assumption of risks to an exception for lands whose rules prohibit it; on such lands it is unclear whether inherent risks remain assumed under this sentence. The two assumption clauses overlap without stating which controls.

The exception for "lands whose rules or regulations prohibit my doing so as a matter of law" identifies no lands, no rules and no decision-maker, so the scope of the assumption of ALL risks cannot be determined from the text. Whether a given course area falls inside the carve-out is left to be proved from outside the document.

An express assumption of ALL risks "inherent or otherwise" cannot be squared with c046, which preserves claims for gross negligence and intentionally wrongful conduct. Read literally this clause would bar the very claims c046 carves out.

The release reaches claims "arising in whole or part from ... enrollment or participation in an activity of NOLS," and "an activity of NOLS" is nowhere defined. Whether free-time conduct, contractor-provided transportation or off-course travel is "an activity of NOLS" is the central undefined term.

The release purports to be given "on behalf of the minor student for whom I sign," which must be read against c003, where the parent's signature is described only as evidence of the Parent's own acknowledgment and agreement. Whether the instrument releases the minor's own claims or only the parent's depends on reconciling the two.

The indemnity runs to claims by "any other person" arising "in whole or part" from an injury suffered by or caused by the student, which on its face would require the student to fund NOLS's defense of claims caused by NOLS's own negligence. The absence of any fault qualifier makes the obligation circular against the release in c044.

The carve-out turns on "gross negligence" and "intentionally wrongful conduct," neither of which is defined or distinguished from the ordinary negligence that is released. Whether pleaded conduct crosses that line decides whether the release applies at all.

The savings statement that the release and indemnity "are intended to be enforced to the fullest extent permitted by law" cannot be squared with c046, which deliberately withholds gross-negligence and intentional-conduct claims from the release. If Wyoming law would permit more, it is unclear whether this sentence expands what c046 expressly limited.

"Lands whose rules or regulations prohibit such agreements as a matter of law" names no lands, no regulations and no mechanism for determining them, so it cannot be told from the text when the release is void. The wording also differs from the parallel carve-out in c043 ("prohibit my doing so"), leaving the two exceptions of uncertain identical scope.

"Or otherwise satisfied NOLS" supplies an alternative to physician verification with no standard for what satisfies NOLS, and "condition that might affect" participation has no boundary. Whether the student breached this representation therefore turns on undefined terms.

"Able to participate without causing harm to myself ... or to others" is an absolute warranty with no standard of measurement or time frame. Any injury on course could be argued to falsify it retrospectively.

"All pertinent medical conditions have been disclosed" leaves "pertinent" undefined and does not say whether pertinence is judged by the student, the physician or NOLS. The warranty's breach turns entirely on that word.

The sentence is passive — "NOLS will be informed" — and names no person who must inform, so it is unclear whether the duty falls on the student, the parent or the physician. It also stops at "prior to the commencement of the course," leaving conditions arising mid-course unaddressed.

Placing responsibility for determining suitability on the student cannot be squared with c055, in which NOLS reserves the right to refuse or remove a student in the student's or the school's best interests. The two allocate the same judgment to different parties.

"For any reason it deems in the best interests of the student or the school" confers unreviewable discretion with no standard, and no consequence (refund, pro-ration) is stated for removal. Whether that discretion is bounded by good faith is left open.

The promise that care "will be provided under the guidance of the NOLS Physician Advisor by way of NOLS' written Medical Protocols" reads as an affirmative undertaking of a standard of care, which sits awkwardly with c053's disclaimer of any representation about managing a medical event. The unincorporated "Medical Protocols" are also never appended or described.

"Pertinent medical information" is undefined and the authorization has no time limit or revocation mechanism. What a third-party provider may lawfully disclose to NOLS is left to that single adjective.

"Costs reasonably associated with medical services, including evacuation" gives no benchmark for reasonableness and does not say whether NOLS's own internal rescue and staff costs are included. The student's exposure under the clause cannot be measured from its words.

"Environmental organizations or strategic partners in which NOLS graduates may be interested" is an open-ended class with no limiting criterion and no consent-withdrawal mechanism. Who qualifies as a "strategic partner" is entirely undefined.

The promotional-use consent for name, contact information and images carries no duration, territory or revocation limit, and does not say whether it survives the course. Its unbounded term is what a court would have to construe.

"Responsible for any damage" states no fault standard, so it is unclear whether the student is liable for accidental or ordinary wear damage as well as negligent damage. "NOLS facilities or gear" also does not say whether it covers gear issued to and carried by the student in the field.

The disclaimer is limited to belongings "stored at NOLS facilities," so by expressio unius nothing is said about personal property lost or damaged in the field or in transit. That omission leaves NOLS's responsibility for field losses open.

The parenthetical "(not including the laws which might apply the laws of another jurisdiction)" is garbled and its intended exclusion of renvoi/conflicts rules must be reconstructed. "Any dispute" is also undefined as to whether it reaches tort and statutory claims as well as contract claims.

"Shall occur or be filed only in the State of Wyoming" does not say whether suit must be in Wyoming state court or may be in the federal court sitting there, and does not say whether mediation is a mandatory condition precedent to suit. The clause's mandatory reach and its forum are both open on these words.

The severability clause must be read against c047 and c048, which respectively demand enforcement to the fullest extent permitted and declare the release wholly void on certain lands; whether an invalid release is severed or merely blue-pencilled is unresolved. The clause does not say whether a partially invalid provision falls entirely or is reformed.

The signature block binds the signers to "THIS PAGE AND THE PREVIOUS 3 PAGES," identifying the agreement by page count rather than by content. If the document as executed is paginated differently, what was agreed to is indeterminate on these words.

The written-modification requirement sits uneasily with c037-c038, which incorporate the NOLS Catalog, website and "other material provided by NOLS" that NOLS can change unilaterally without any signed writing. Whether such changed material alters the parties' terms cannot be answered from either provision alone.
